paragraphs.zh: The Chinese patent application, CN106565561A discloses a process for the preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoyl benzoyl chloride. In the process of preparing 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoyl benzoyl chloride, a step of oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyltoluene (NMST) is carried out in presence of nitric acid using vanadium pentoxide as a catalyst to obtain 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid (NMSBA).
paragraphs.en: The Chinese patent application, CN106565561A discloses a process for the preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoyl benzoyl chloride. In the process of preparing 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoyl benzoyl chloride, a step of oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyltoluene (NMST) is carried out in presence of nitric acid using vanadium pentoxide as a catalyst to obtain 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid (NMSBA).

paragraphs.zh: However, the processes known in the art for preparing mesotrione and its intermediate involve tedious procedures, e.g. a relatively greater number of steps, which includes conversion of NMSBA to NMSBC, as well as isolation and purification of intermediates at each step. This result in excessive production time, which in turn renders the processes more costly and less eco-friendly, thus the processes are not suitable for commercial scale up. The known processes further involve use of high amount of solvents that leads to production of high volume of effluent.

drawings.notes: One scheme, one arrow, two structures. Printed labels, recorded per brief section 8: 'NMST' is printed centred under the LEFT structure and 'NMSBA' centred under the RIGHT structure. No formula number (no 'Formula II' or similar) is printed anywhere in this drawing. Both labels are set in the serif body face while the atom labels are sans serif, so the labels are typeset captions rather than part of the drawn graphic. Substituent positions were read off the drawing at 4x, not inferred from the names in the prose: in both structures the hexagon is drawn point-up, the C1 substituent (CH3 on the left structure, the carboxyl carbon on the right) hangs off the top vertex, NO2 off the upper-right vertex which is therefore C2, and SO2 off the bottom vertex which is therefore C4, with the S-methyl drawn down and to the left as H3C. Kekule pattern is an ordinary benzene in both, double bonds C1=C2, C3=C4, C5=C6. Ink on this page is clean and solid, NOT the broken dotted ink the brief reports for p15, and the arrow is a single solid shaft with one solid filled arrowhead pointing right. Above and below the arrow are kept separate per prompt rule 6: 'Nitric acid' and 'V2O5' are stacked on two lines ABOVE the shaft, '140-150°C' is BELOW it. Measured on the image, the degree sign is printed closed up with no space before it: the gap between the final 0 and the degree ring is 3 pixels, the same as the other inter-glyph gaps in that string, where a word space at this size would be 8 pixels or more. presented_as is prior_art: the scheme sits inside BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION and illustrates the process of the third-party Chinese application CN106565561A named in [009] immediately above it, so it is somebody else's route and not the route of this disclosure. Note that prior_art here describes how the page presents the scheme, not the chemical role of NMST and NMSBA, which are in fact intermediates on the invention's own route later in the document.

discrepancies.what: The drawn arrow carries a reaction temperature that the prose beside it does not mention.
discrepancies.text_says: [009] gives the reagents (nitric acid, vanadium pentoxide as catalyst) but states no temperature anywhere for the oxidation, nor anywhere else on the page.

discrepancies.what: The prose describes the cited process as making a benzoyl chloride, but the drawn scheme stops one step earlier at the carboxylic acid and draws no chlorination.
discrepancies.drawing_says: A single arrow, NMST to NMSBA. No acid chloride is drawn and no chlorinating agent appears.
discrepancies.text_says: [009] says CN106565561A 'discloses a process for the preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoyl benzoyl chloride', and describes the drawn oxidation as only 'a step' within that process.

discrepancies.what: The same moiety is spelled a third way on this page, unlike either of the two spellings the brief records.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The drawing spells nothing out; it uses only the abbreviations NMST and NMSBA and the atom labels CH3, NO2, SO2, H3C, OH, O.
discrepancies.text_says: [009] prints 'methylsulfonyl' with an f AND closed up against the next fragment with no space, three times: '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoyl', '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyltoluene', '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid'. The brief's section 8 lists the space-separated forms '2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl toluene' and '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl benzoic acid'. Recorded, not normalised, and not reconciled.
